title: Precision stress test + fallback matrix — Optimize console walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked HelixCare through the Optimize console quantization profiles, demonstrated an INT8/FP8 stress test and fallback matrix, discussed quality vs latency metrics and runbook for automated fallbacks. Customer requested sandbox access, benchmark sheet, and a 1-week stress pilot. Several security and rollout questions raised (KMS, VPC).
action_items: Jordan Kim - Share sandbox credentials and guide - 2027-02-17
Priya Nair - Export the latency/fidelity benchmark spreadsheet and sample qprofiles - 2027-02-16
Tom Bauer - Provide sample prompts and SLO targets for the pilot - 2027-02-18
next_steps: Grant HelixCare sandbox (Optimize + Console) and send quant checklist
Run a 1-week stress pilot starting 2027-02-21 with provided prompts
Follow up call to review pilot results and fallback triggers week of 2027-02-28
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Product), Alicia Ramos (CTO, HelixCare), Tom Bauer (ML Platform Lead), Neha Singh (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): Walkthrough of Optimize quant profiles, showed INT8/FP8 profiles, ran a stress test in sandbox, discussed automated fallback rules and a matrix for quality thresholds.

[00:00] Jordan: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round — I'm Jordan, AE on the account. Priya and Marcus from the SE/product side. You folks at HelixCare?
[00:12] Alicia: Hi, Alicia here, CTO. We are particularly interested in lowering token cost without losing clinical fidelity.
[00:19] Tom: Tom, ML infra. Our SLO is 250ms p95 for short queries, but we can accept some tail for longer docs.
[00:28] Priya: Great, that's helpful. Today we'll show the Optimize console, run a precision stress test across INT8 and FP8, and then sketch a fallback matrix — when to fallback to a higher-precision model or a hosted variant.
[00:41] Marcus: Also point out how caching and batching interact with qprofiles — since HelixCare is latency-sensitive, we want to show the end-to-end numbers not just per-token.
[00:51] Jordan: Cool, quick note: transcription might mess up some acronyms — K-V cache sometimes shows up as K-V cash in exports — apologies in advance.
[00:58] (laughter)
[01:03] Priya: Alright, I'm sharing my screen. This is the Optimize console -> Profiles tab. On the left are pre-built qprofiles, we have one labeled clinical-conservative-int8, one labeled clinical-balanced-fp8, and a fallback policy attached.
[01:19] Alicia: Can you explain what you mean by "fallback policy"?
[01:22] Priya: Sure, it's a set of rules: quality threshold (measured by our evaluation hooks, e.g., BLEU/ROUGE or custom prompt checks), latency threshold, and a confidence metric from the model. If e.g., clinical-conservative-int8 drops below 0.92 fidelity on our held-out prompts, the orchestrator will route to clinical-balanced-fp8 or the hosted-highfidelity model depending on capacity.
[01:44] Tom: How do you compute "fidelity"? Is that automated?
[01:48] Priya: We plug in your prompt set and run automatic evals in the Optimize sandbox. There's a stability score which combines semantic similarity, hallucination heuristics, and a domain-specific scorer you can upload. It's semi-automated — you can review flagged prompts.
[02:03] Neha: Does this require sending PII to Redwood? We have constraints.
[02:07] Jordan: Good question — for the pilot we recommend synthetic prompts, but we also support VPC/private deployments and customer-managed KMS for Private customers. For hosted sandboxes we offer redaction hooks and short retention. We'll send the security note after this call.
[02:20] Alicia: Okay that helps.
[02:24] Priya: I'm going to run a short stress script: 1k sequential short queries and then a burst of 200 concurrent requests. This will show p50/p95 latency and fidelity regression for INT8 and FP8. Note: our sandbox is scaled for demo loads, not production throughput.
[02:39] [00:03:10] (screen activity)
[02:43] Priya: Starting INT8 run now. You can see the live chart — p50 around 120ms, p95 around 280ms for short prompts. Fidelity on our clinical prompt set is 0.91 according to the default scorer.
[02:55] Tom: 0.91 — that's a touch under our 0.92 bar, right?
[02:58] Alicia: Yes we'd prefer 0.93 ideally.
[03:01] Priya: Understood. I'm triggering the fallback matrix now: rule is if fidelity < 0.92 for five-minute window AND p95 < 500ms, then route to FP8-balanced.
[03:14] [00:04:25] Priya: FP8 run — p50 ~ 150ms, p95 ~ 320ms, fidelity 0.94. So FP8 improves fidelity but increases tail latency slightly.
[03:27] Marcus: Important to note that quantization profile affects KV cache hit behavior; some of our kernels optimize repeated context but for FP8 the execution path slightly increases memory and eviction, which contributes to tail.
[03:41] Neha: Are there any unexpected regressions we should watch for? E.g., tokenization or numeric stability?
[03:47] Priya: Good call. We've seen numerical noise on a few edge prompts; Optimize flags those with a 'sensitivity' tag. We recommend doing a short sensitivity sweep over your most critical prompts as part of the pilot.
[03:59] Tom: Can the system automatically roll back if fidelity drops mid-run?
[04:03] Jordan: Yes — the orchestrator supports automatic fallback and can also do canary rollouts with percent traffic. You can configure time-based cooldowns so it doesn't thrash.
[04:13] Alicia: How do we tune the thresholds without false positives? We don't want unnecessary fallbacks that increase cost.
[04:18] Priya: We suggest a three-stage approach: 1) run baseline metrics on your prompt set, 2) run a stress phase with simulated traffic to observe variance, 3) set thresholds at 2-3 sigma from baseline and run canary traffic at 5-10% to validate. The console shows recommended thresholds based on observed distributions.
[04:37] [00:05:00] (typing)
[04:40] Marcus: Also, Optimize records a cost delta for each fallback decision so you can evaluate unit economics over time. We can surface monthly cost estimates for the pilot.
[04:50] Tom: Good. Could you show what the fallback matrix looks like as a table?
[04:54] Priya: Sure — this is live in the console. Column A is condition (fidelity, latency, confidence), Column B is action (route to FP8-balanced, route to hosted-highfi, throttle), Column C is cooldown and owner.
[05:07] Priya: For HelixCare we sketched: fidelity<0.92 => FP8-balanced; fidelity<0.88 => hosted-highfi + slack to product team; latency>800ms p95 => throttle and queue with burst path to Dedicated pool if enrolled.
[05:23] Alicia: If we go Dedicated later, would the same qprofiles transfer?
[05:27] Marcus: Yes, profiles and rollouts are portable — the same Optimize config can be applied to Dedicated or Private, although kernel selections may change slightly depending on hardware.
[05:36] Neha: Regarding keys and logs — we need audit logs and KMS integration. Is that available for the sandbox?
[05:41] Jordan: Sandbox has limited logs. For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS, full audit logs, and SSO/SAML. We'll attach the security pack after.
[05:51] (short silence)
[05:56] Priya: I'm going to run one of the sensitivity sweeps now — this is a short set of 30 edge prompts that often detect hallucination drift under INT8.
[06:05] [00:06:30] (run results)
[06:09] Priya: Sweep shows 4 prompts flagged for hallucination-heuristic; two of those flip to correct under FP8. So this is a signal to include those prompts in the guardrail list.
[06:20] Tom: Makes sense. We have a shortlist of 40 test prompts; we'll send those tonight.
[06:24] Jordan: Great — we'll ingest them and include in the pilot config.
[06:28] Alicia: On billing — if we start with hosted sandbox then move to Dedicated, is there migration cost?
[06:33] Marcus: Minimal. Billing shifts from per-token to reserved capacity pricing. We can provide comparative cost model for your observed request mix. We'll include that in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:44] (background noise)
[06:48] Priya: Quick demo of the API-level override: you can annotate requests that require high fidelity and force a high-fidelity route, or tag them for audit. This integrates with SDKs and our streaming endpoints.
[06:59] Neha: Do overrides bypass automatic fallbacks?
[07:02] Priya: Overrides are honoring — they will route to the specified profile but they're still subject to capacity-based fallback if the node is out of resources.
[07:12] Alicia: Can we get logs for fallbacks so our SREs can analyze patterns?
[07:16] Jordan: Yes — fallback events are emitted to the event stream and can be forwarded to your Splunk/Datadog/S3. We'll send sample log schema.
[07:26] (crosstalk)
[07:30] Marcus: We're about 40 minutes in. Quick recap and next steps?
[07:34] Jordan: Recap: 1) Priya showed INT8/FP8 runs, FP8 recovers fidelity but with slightly higher p95. 2) We sketched fallback matrix and runbook. 3) Action: Redwood to provide sandbox, benchmark sheet, and ingest HelixCare prompts.
[07:49] Alicia: Good. I'd like the first pilot to prioritize patient-facing summarization prompts. That's our biggest risk area.
[07:56] Tom: We'll share SLOs and the 40 prompt set by EOD.
[07:59] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[08:02] Neha: One ask — can we get an example sensitivity report format?
[08:06] Priya: Yes, we'll include an example PDF and the raw CSV from today's runs.
[08:10] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the security pack.
[08:15] Alicia: Thanks all.
[08:18] (meeting ends)

End of transcript.
